title: What Plants Need and Animal Habitats
seo_title: Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology: What Plants Need and Animal Habitats Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology: What plants need to grow; habitats of animals
standard_text: Plants need light, water, air and nutrients to grow. A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives and gets food, water and shelter. Animals build shelters, such as nests, burrows and webs. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 4, Life and Living: What plants need to grow; habitats of animals)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): what plants need to grow, habitats, animal shelters and how living things suit their habitats. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants need light, water, air and nutrients.
key_sub: A habitat gives food, water and shelter.
body_html:
How to think about it

Green plants need sunlight, water, air (carbon dioxide) and nutrients from the soil to grow well. A plant kept in the dark grows pale and weak; a plant without water wilts.

A habitat is where a plant or animal lives. It gives food, water, shelter and a place to raise young. Animals build shelters such as weaver nests, termite mounds, burrows and spider webs. Living things have features that suit their habitat.

Example

A plant on a dark shelf grows pale and thin. What is it missing?

What do leaves need?

Answer: light

Example

A meerkat lives underground. What kind of shelter is this?

A tunnel in the ground

Answer: a burrow

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking a habitat is only a house built by people.
  • Forgetting that plants need air.

faq.q: Why does a weaver bird build its nest at the end of a branch?
faq.a: Snakes and other predators find it hard to reach.

faq.q: Can two animals share a habitat?
faq.a: Yes. A habitat is home to many kinds of plants and animals.

items.q: A red zebra has long, strong back legs. How does this feature help it survive?
c: to lose heat and hear predators at night

items.q: A spinifex hopping mouse has long back legs and a long tail. How does this feature help it survive?

items.q: Which structural feature helps a red zebra survive in its habitat?

items.q: Which of these is a behavioural adaptation?

items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.
